name: Palak Paneer

ingredients.name: Spinach (palak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium bunch; about 4 packed cups of leaves

ingredients.name: Ice cubes + cold water (for chilling spinach)

equipment: Saucepan or patila (1.5–2 litre) for blanching
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)

steps.title: Pick the spinach
steps.text: Pull 150 g spinach leaves off the bunch, keeping only the thin tender stems. Throw away thick stalks and yellow or damaged leaves.
steps.visualCue: a pile of whole, dark-green leaves with only short, thin stems and no yellow patches
steps.cameraCheck: the picked leaves next to the discarded stalks
steps.videoShot: hand snapping leaves off thick stems
steps.watchOut: thick, mature stalks and old leaves make the gravy bitter; if a stem does not bend easily when you fold it, pull it off and bin it.

steps.title: Wash the spinach
steps.text: Put the leaves in a big bowl of water, swish, lift them out, and repeat with fresh water 2–3 times.
steps.visualCue: no sand or soil settled at the bottom of the bowl on the last wash
steps.cameraCheck: clean water at the bottom of the bowl
steps.videoShot: leaves lifted out of the water by hand
steps.watchOut: grit shows as a gritty crunch in the finished curry; if you still see sand in the last bowl, wash once more (pour the water off gently instead of tipping the leaves out with it).

steps.title: Boil water
steps.text: Put 750 ml (3 cups) water in the saucepan on high heat.
steps.visualCue: big, rolling bubbles that keep going when you stir
steps.cameraCheck: the saucepan at a rolling boil
steps.videoShot: water bubbling hard
steps.watchOut: if the water is only steaming or has small bubbles, the spinach takes too long to wilt and turns dull; wait for the full rolling boil.

steps.title: Make the ice bath
steps.text: Fill a bowl with 500 ml cold water and 6–8 ice cubes.
steps.visualCue: ice cubes floating in clearly cold water
steps.videoShot: ice cubes dropped into water
steps.watchOut: too little ice and the water warms up at once, so the spinach keeps cooking and loses colour; if the ice melts fast, add more cubes or swap the water.

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces, each smaller than a pea
steps.videoShot: knife chopping onion finely
steps.watchOut: big pieces stay crunchy and raw-tasting in a smooth gravy; if any piece is bigger than a pea, chop it again.

steps.title: Chop tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 60 g (1 small) tomato.
steps.visualCue: small juicy pieces with the seeds mixed in
steps.videoShot: tomato diced on the board
steps.watchOut: large chunks take longer to melt, so the gravy tastes raw and sour; chop small.

steps.title: Prep ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Peel and roughly chop 5 g ginger and 2 garlic cloves. Slit 1 green chilli and remove the stem.
steps.visualCue: three small heaps on the board
steps.cameraCheck: ginger, garlic and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: garlic cloves being peeled and chopped
steps.watchOut: chilli oils burn eyes; wash your hands before touching your face. Removing the seeds makes the curry milder.

steps.title: Cube and soak paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes and cover with warm (not boiling) water.
steps.visualCue: even cubes fully under the water
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of paneer cubes in water
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes slid into warm water
steps.watchOut: boiling water makes paneer tough and rubbery; the water should feel comfortably warm to a finger.

steps.title: Blanch the spinach
steps.text: Push the spinach leaves into the boiling water with a spoon so they are all under.
steps.visualCue: leaves are limp and a bright, vivid green; stems bend easily
steps.cameraCheck: the pot of bright-green wilted leaves
steps.videoShot: leaves sinking and wilting in boiling water
steps.watchOut: past about 2–3 minutes the colour turns dull olive and the taste gets bitter; once it has gone dull the colour cannot be rescued, so lift the leaves out the moment they are limp.

steps.title: Chill the spinach
steps.text: Lift the spinach out with a slotted spoon (or drain) and drop it straight into the ice water.
steps.visualCue: leaves are cold to the touch and stay bright green
steps.cameraCheck: green leaves in the ice bowl
steps.videoShot: steaming leaves plunged into ice water
steps.watchOut: if the water turns warm and the leaves stay hot, they keep cooking and darken; add more ice or change the water.

steps.title: Squeeze the spinach
steps.text: Lift the leaves out and gently squeeze out the extra water with your hands.
steps.visualCue: a compact green ball that no longer drips
steps.cameraCheck: the squeezed spinach ball in your palm
steps.videoShot: hands pressing water from the spinach
steps.watchOut: leftover water makes the gravy thin and pale; if water runs between your fingers, squeeze again.

steps.title: Blend the purée
steps.text: Put the spinach, ginger, garlic and green chilli in the small mixer jar with 2 tbsp of the ice water and blend until smooth.
steps.tip: blend in short bursts so the motor heat doesn't dull the colour.
steps.visualCue: thick, smooth, bright-green purée with only tiny flecks
steps.videoShot: green purée being scraped down the jar
steps.watchOut: too much water gives a thin gravy, and long non-stop blending warms and dulls the colour; if the purée is gritty, blend in short bursts and scrape the jar down.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: oil swirling in the kadai
steps.watchOut: oil that smokes is too hot and tastes burnt; take the pan off the heat for 20 seconds and lower the flame.

steps.title: Temper cumin
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.visualCue: seeds sizzle and turn a shade darker; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: cumin crackling in oil
steps.watchOut: cumin goes from brown to black and bitter within seconds; if it turns black, tip it out and start again with fresh seeds.

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: soft, translucent and light golden at the edges, with a sweet smell
steps.videoShot: onion sizzling as it's stirred
steps.watchOut: dark brown onion turns the gravy brown and bitter; if it browns too fast, lower the heat and sprinkle 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and a pinch of the salt and stir.
steps.visualCue: tomato turns mushy and the mix looks jammy, with oil starting to show at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, pressing tomato with the spatula
steps.videoShot: spatula squashing soft tomato
steps.watchOut: a raw, sharp tomato smell means it needs another minute; the acid of undercooked tomato can also dull the green later.

steps.title: Add spice powders
steps.text: Lower the heat. Add the pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ½ tsp coriander powder and stir.
steps.tip: if it starts sticking, add 1 tbsp water instead of more oil.
steps.visualCue: masala turns reddish and smells toasty
steps.videoShot: spices sprinkled and stirred in
steps.watchOut: powders burn in seconds and taste bitter; if the masala sticks or darkens, add 1 tbsp water at once.

steps.title: Add spinach purée
steps.text: Pour in the spinach purée and stir it into the masala.
steps.visualCue: evenly green gravy with flecks of onion and no white or red streaks
steps.videoShot: green purée poured into the masala
steps.watchOut: the purée splatters on a hot pan; keep the heat low and stir straight away so it does not catch on the bottom.

steps.title: Loosen with water
steps.text: Add 60 ml (¼ cup) water and the rest of the salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: gravy flows slowly off the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: the spatula lifted out of the gravy
steps.videoShot: gravy dripping off the spatula
steps.watchOut: too much water makes a thin, pale gravy and too little a thick paste; if thin, simmer uncovered a little longer, and if thick, add 1–2 tbsp water.

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Simmer on low, partly covered (it splutters).
steps.tip: don't cook longer than about 4 minutes, or the colour goes dull.
steps.visualCue: gentle bubbles; still bright green and slightly thicker
steps.videoShot: green gravy bubbling lazily
steps.watchOut: a hard boil or more than about 4 minutes turns the colour dull olive; keep the bubbles lazy and stop at 3 minutes.

steps.title: Add paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Fold gently.
steps.visualCue: every cube coated in green gravy
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes folded into the gravy
steps.watchOut: rough stirring crumbles the cubes; fold with the spatula rather than stir.

steps.title: Simmer paneer
steps.text: Simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: paneer is warmed through and soft, with slow bubbles around the cubes
steps.videoShot: slow bubbles around white paneer cubes
steps.watchOut: longer than 3 minutes makes paneer chewy; if a cube feels hard when pressed with the spatula, it is already overcooked (a splash of water and the cream later will soften the taste, not the texture).

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: a "restaurant-like" aroma fills the kitchen
steps.videoShot: kasuri methi crushed between palms
steps.watchOut: burnt kasuri methi is bitter, so add it only at this late stage and do not fry it; if you smell burning, take the pan off the heat.

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed, with a warm spice smell
steps.videoShot: garam masala sprinkled over
steps.watchOut: too much garam masala overpowers the spinach and tastes harsh; stay at ¼ tsp.

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Swirl in 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh cream.
steps.tip: adding cream with the heat off stops it splitting.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a lighter, glossy green
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through green gravy
steps.watchOut: cream added over high heat or boiled afterwards splits into oily streaks; if it splits, take the pan off the heat and stir in 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Taste and plate
steps.text: Taste; add ½ tsp lemon juice if it tastes flat (optional). Spoon into a bowl, with a small swirl of cream on top if you like.
steps.visualCue: bright-green curry with white paneer cubes
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl
steps.watchOut: too much lemon makes it sour and can dull the green; add a few drops, stir and taste before adding more.

reasons: A big portion of leafy greens (150 g spinach) gives fibre, folate, vitamin A and K and some iron, and paneer adds about 18 g of protein and plenty of calcium. Nothing is fried and there is no added sugar. Fat is still fairly high (about 35 g, with about 16 g saturated from paneer and cream) and sodium is about 940 mg. Restaurant versions often use more cream and butter, fry the paneer, and add more salt.

researchRating.basis: one of the most-loved North Indian vegetarian curries, with consistently high recipe ratings (4.66 to 5 across the sites checked; several have few votes). Recurring complaints are a bitter or "metallic" taste and dull brown-green colour when the spinach is overcooked, mature, or reheated, and a commenter on Manjula's Kitchen reported dull, dark greens when the spinach was not blanched.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 1–2 days (est.); the colour dulls and the spinach taste gets stronger with each day. Freezer: the spinach gravy alone (without paneer and cream) freezes for up to 1 month (est.); add fresh paneer when reheating. Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 1–2 tbsp water, stirring, just until hot. Don't boil or reheat more than once: repeated heating makes it more bitter and brown.
leftoverRemix: Palak paneer stuffed paratha. Cook the leftover curry down until thick and dry, mash the paneer into it, cool, then stuff into atta dough and roll out into parathas. Cook on a tawa with a few drops of oil and serve with curd.
burnOff: about 6.7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 9.4 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).

navratri.reason: skip onion, garlic, kasuri methi and garam masala, and use sendha namak and ghee; assumes paneer and leafy greens are allowed (common rule set; families differ)

ekadashi.reason: skip onion, garlic and kasuri methi, and eat it without roti or rice (grains are commonly avoided; common rule set assumed, families differ)

jain.reason: drop onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots); use sonth and hing

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; fine at iftar or sehri with roti, though fairly rich (about 16 g saturated fat) and the spinach adds iron

jain.reason: drop the onion (40 g), garlic (6 g) and fresh ginger (5 g), which are roots under the Patch 05 rule; use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) and hing (check it is gluten-free if that matters) instead (see Jain variant)

vegan.reason: the dish is defined by paneer (100 g) and fresh cream (15 ml); a tofu version is a different dish and was not researched

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: skip the onion (40 g) and garlic (6 g); use extra tomato and a little more ginger (see Sattvik variant)

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or hing in this recipe (check the garam masala pack; some blends contain compounded hing); serve with rice or a gluten-free roti, not wheat roti

dairyFree.reason: paneer (100 g) and fresh cream (15 ml) are dairy

variants.reason: the dish is defined by paneer and cream; a tofu or cashew version is a different dish and was not researched
